results.evidence: The exhibit openly frames the 26% ORR as interim single-arm data from a registrational trial and explicitly contrasts it against docetaxel SOC's 12.8% ORR as external benchmark — the open-label/single-arm nature is disclosed, not masked. The registry confirms the trial is non-randomized with ORR as primary endpoint, matching what the company presents; there is no over-reach placing a non-primary basis into the success slot.

The exhibit explicitly contextualizes the ~26% ORR / mDOR figure as interim Phase 2 single-arm data (footnote 3: 'Interim data cut as of October 10, 2025') and juxtaposes it against a clearly labeled SOC benchmark (~13% ORR; ~8mo mDOR; ~13mo mOS) on the same slide. The 'potential best-in-class' framing is hedged ('Potential') and the comparator basis is disclosed, not masked — readers can see this is uncontrolled single-arm data versus a historical SOC reference.

The exhibit openly labels the supporting data as single-arm interim results from IOV-LUN-202 with n=39, 25.6% ORR, and mDOR not reached at 25.4 months median follow-up, and explicitly shows the anti-PD-1 ORR benchmarks it is comparing against. The trial design slide states the primary endpoint is ORR by IRC and identifies the cohorts and population — the single-arm/open-label nature is disclosed, not concealed. 'Unprecedented durability' is marketing puffery tied to disclosed mDOR-not-reached data, not a masked endpoint substitution for the catalyst.

The flagged quote 'Unprecedented Durability' is not located verbatim in the restored exhibit excerpt — only the forward-looking statements boilerplate is shown, so we cannot verify whether the claim was made in the success-determining slot for NCT04614103 or whether it carried qualifying context (e.g., attribution to melanoma data, n-size, follow-up caveats). The registry confirms the trial is single-arm Phase 2 with ORR as primary, which makes a durability overreach plausible in principle, but absence of the actual claim text in the exhibit prevents confirmation that marketing positioned durability as the success basis for this catalyst.

The exhibit explicitly labels this as 'Interim data cut as of October 10, 2025' from a single-arm registrational cohort, alongside the disclosed primary endpoint (ORR by IRC) and a 25.6% ORR with n=39. The mDOR-not-reached figure is presented as descriptive durability with median follow-up disclosed (25.4 months), not as a controlled treatment-effect claim — consistent with the registry's single-arm non-randomized design that everyone reading the slide can see.

The exhibit immediately substantiates the 'potentially best-in-class' framing with the specific interim numbers (ORR 26%, mDOR not reached at >25 months) and discloses that the trial is ongoing with updated data due in 2026. The qualifier 'potentially' and the disclosed single-arm interim nature mean the marketing is contextualized rather than masking a controlled comparison; the first pass severed the surrounding numeric disclosure and forward-looking framing.

The exhibit explicitly labels the data as 'Strong Preliminary Clinical Results' from open-label registrational Cohorts 1 and 2 with n=23 evaluable patients, discloses the 26.1% ORR, notes responses were investigator-assessed, and gives the data cut date — the single-arm nature is openly disclosed, not masked. The registry primary endpoint (ORR) matches what the exhibit reports, and the 'deep, durable responses' phrasing is standard descriptive language for a single-arm Phase 2 with disclosed n and DOR figures (71% with DOR ≥6 months).

The exhibit clearly frames this as preliminary single-arm Phase 2 interim data with data cut July 6, 2023, n=23 patients, ORR 26.1% by RECIST 1.1, assessed by investigator — it is openly presented as descriptive durability from a non-randomized registrational cohort, not as a controlled efficacy claim. The trial design slide on the prior page explicitly states primary endpoint is ORR by IRC in a Phase 2 multicenter single-arm study, so 'all responses ongoing' is a transparent durability descriptor consistent with the registered design, not an overreach into a success-determining slot.

The exhibit clearly frames the data as 'Preliminary Clinical Results for IOV-LUN-202 Cohorts 1 and 2' with a July 6, 2023 data cut, n=23, and explicitly reports ORR 26.1% (95% CI 10.2, 48.4) as the efficacy readout — the durability statement is a descriptive observation about a swimmer's plot, not a substitute for the primary ORR endpoint. The registry primary is ORR, which the exhibit reports directly, so there is no over-reach into the success-determining slot.
